title: G-rings tested by finite domain generic formal fibres
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian semilocal ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where semilocal means having finitely many maximal ideals. Then $R$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] if and only if the following condition holds. For every commutative $R$-algebra $B$ that is a nonzero integral domain and finite as an $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] (such a $B$ is Noetherian semilocal), let $\mathfrak r_B$ be the intersection of its maximal ideals and let $C=\varprojlim_n B/\mathfrak r_B^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For every prime $\mathfrak P\subset C$ whose inverse image in $B$ is $(0)$, the local ring $C_{\mathfrak P}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The finite algebra map $R\to B$ need not be injective. No characteristic or universal catenarity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Rotthaus, Komplettierung semilokaler quasiausgezeichneter Ringe, Nagoya Math. J. 76 (1979), Lemma 1(a)–(b), p.174 (Matsumura 33.E); her terminology quasiausgezeichnet means geometrically regular formal fibres, as explicitly defined on p.173. Related Stacks Tag 07PQ, more-algebra-lemma-check-G-ring, is the finite-free regular-formal-fibre test, not this finite-domain generic-fibre formulation.

proof.text: First check the parenthetical assertion about a finite $R$-algebra $B$. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian]. It is integral over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], so every maximal ideal of $B$ contracts to a maximal ideal of $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-extension-dimension]. Over each such ideal there are finitely many primes by the finiteness assertion in [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension]. There are finitely many maximal ideals of $R$, hence finitely many maximal ideals of $B$. This reasoning does not assume that $R\to B$ is injective. If $R$ is the zero ring there is no unital map to a nonzero domain; its G-ring condition is vacuous as well, by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Henceforth take $R\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 07PQ, algebraic finiteness preliminaries; algebra.tex Tags 00FN, 00OJ and 07N9.

proof.text: For the forward direction assume $R$ is a G-ring. Module generators of $B$ also generate it as an $R$-algebra, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-g-ring] makes $B$ a G-ring. By [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-completion-regular], $B\to C$ is regular for its Jacobson-radical completion. Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$. Its fibre $F=C\otimes_BK$ over $(0)$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular. Taking the trivial field extension in [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] makes $F$ regular. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], $F=(B\setminus\{0\})^{-1}C$. A prime $\mathfrak P$ of $C$ contracting to zero is disjoint from this denominator set, and $F_{\mathfrak P F}\cong C_{\mathfrak P}$: the isomorphism sends $(c/s)/(d/u)$ to $cu/(sd)$ and has inverse $c/d\mapsto(c/1)/(d/1)$. The definition [def-weil-regular-scheme] therefore gives the required regular local ring.

source.place: Tags 07PQ (forward implication), 07PV and 0AH2; algebra.tex, geometric regularity Definition 0382.

proof.text: Assume now the stated test on finite domain algebras. Fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$, a prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak m$, and a finite purely inseparable extension $L/K$, where $A=R/\mathfrak q$ and $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Construct a finite domain $R$-algebra $B\subset L$ with fraction field $L$ as follows. In characteristic zero take $B=A$, since $L=K$ by [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. In characteristic $p>0$, choose a finite $K$-basis $u_1,\ldots,u_s$ of $L$. For each $j$ choose $e_j\geq0$ and $a_j,b_j\in A$, $b_j\ne0$, with $u_j^{p^{e_j}}=a_j/b_j$. For $d=\prod_jb_j$ and $v_j=du_j$, one has $v_j^{p^{e_j}}=d^{p^{e_j}}a_j/b_j\in A$. Thus $v_j$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $A$. Set $B=A[v_1,\ldots,v_s]\subset L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators] it is finite over $A$. Since $A$ is cyclic over $R$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-over-finite-algebra] makes it finite over $R$. It is a nonzero domain. Moreover $K\subseteq\operatorname{Frac}(B)\subseteq L$ and $u_j=v_j/d$ lies in $\operatorname{Frac}(B)$; the basis then gives equality. Step 1 applies to $B$.

source.place: Tag 07PQ, construction of a finite model for a prescribed purely inseparable residue-field extension; denominator-clearing variant of its finite-free model. The monic calculation is written out here.

proof.text: Let $C_B$ be the Jacobson-radical completion of this $B$. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]. Put $S=B\setminus\{0\}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], $G=C_B\otimes_BL=S^{-1}C_B$, because $L=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$. This is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Its prime ideals correspond to primes $\mathfrak P\subset C_B$ disjoint from $S$, equivalently contracting to zero in $B$. As in Step 2 its local ring is $(C_B)_{\mathfrak P}$, regular by the assumed test. Hence $G$ is regular by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Apply [lem-per-semilocal-jacobson-completion-product] to $B$ and invert $S$. This gives $G\cong\prod_{\mathfrak n\in\operatorname{Max}B}(\widehat{B_{\mathfrak n}}\otimes_BL)$. Localization commutes with this finite product: on each component it sends $(c_{\mathfrak n})/s$ to $(c_{\mathfrak n}/s)$, and component fractions have a common denominator obtained by multiplying their finitely many denominators. Thus each factor is regular. Indeed primes in a finite product select exactly one of its orthogonal coordinate idempotents, so the corresponding local ring equals a local ring of that factor; each factor is also a quotient of the Noetherian product.

source.place: Tag 07PQ, regular generic fibres of the finite models; algebra.tex Tag 07N9 proof, via the separately stated semilocal completion comparison.

proof.text: Write $H=\widehat{R_{\mathfrak m}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension], $H\otimes_RB\cong\prod_{\mathfrak n\cap R=\mathfrak m}\widehat{B_{\mathfrak n}}$ as $B$-algebras. All these $\mathfrak n$ are maximal: their quotients are domains integral over $R/\mathfrak m$, a field, and a nonzero element integral over a field has its inverse expressed by its monic equation with nonzero constant coefficient. Hence they occur among the factors of Step 4. Tensor with $L$ over $B$ and use [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] (and the interchange of tensor factors). Since $L$ is the localization of $B$ at $S$, the common-denominator calculation of Step 4 identifies the result with the finite product of $\widehat{B_{\mathfrak n}}\otimes_BL$. Consequently $H\otimes_RL$ is regular: at every prime its local ring is that of one regular factor, and this finite product is Noetherian, since an ideal is the product of its finitely many coordinate ideals, whose finite generators can be put in their respective coordinates. The empty product is the zero ring, also regular.

source.place: Tag 07PQ, displayed completion/base-change product in the converse; algebra.tex Tag 07N9 (algebra-lemma-completion-finite-extension).

proof.text: For fixed $\mathfrak m,\mathfrak q$, put $F=H\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. The completion $H$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], and $F$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-noetherian]. For every finite purely inseparable $L/\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, Step 5 gives regularity of $F\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}L\cong H\otimes_RL$, the cancellation isomorphism sending $(h\otimes a)\otimes l$ to $h\otimes al$. Thus $F$ is geometrically regular by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. The primes of $R_{\mathfrak m}$ are precisely $\mathfrak qR_{\mathfrak m}$ for $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak m$, with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$; contraction sends a prime $Q$ to $\mathfrak q$, while membership $a/s\in Q$ is equivalent to $a/1\in Q$ since $s/1$ is a unit; conversely extension of a prime disjoint from the denominators is prime. Residue fields are identified by $a/s\mapsto\bar a/\bar s$. With the conventions of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], the fibre of $R_{\mathfrak m}\to H$ is exactly $F$, since every element outside $\mathfrak m$ is already a unit in both tensor factors. This completion map is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat]. Its fibres are therefore Noetherian and geometrically regular, so it is regular. This holds for every maximal $\mathfrak m$, and [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-maximal-ideal-criterion] concludes that $R$ is a G-ring.

Step 2: forward direction by 07PV and 0AH2 (any ideal, here r_B); the trivial extension k'=k gives regularity; F=S^-1 C via 00DK, with the explicit fraction isomorphism to C_P. Step 3: v_j=d u_j has v_j^{p^e} = (d^{p^e}/b_j) a_j in A, so B=A[v] is finite over A, then over R; Frac B = L; no Nagata assumption. Step 4: G = S^-1 C_B is Noetherian, and its primes are exactly those of C_B contracting to 0, so it is regular by the test. The new node is then applied to B (semilocal by step 1), and the factors are regular via finite-product localization. Step 5: 07N9 at m, primes over m are maximal, tensor-cancel gives H⊗_R L as a finite regular product (empty product handled). Step 6: F is Noetherian, F⊗L ≅ H⊗_R L is regular for every finite purely inseparable L, so F is geometrically regular. The fibre of R_m -> H at qR_m is F, the map is flat by 00MB, and 07PT concludes.
